asr_text: The safety reports draw a line here. A 2025 international report said existing systems were not able to undermine human control in a meaningful way at the time of that report. A later report described a severe loss of control scenario as requiring three things together: enough ability, a harmful tendency to use it, and a setting that gives the system access and opportunity. It says experts do not agree on the exact mix. Warnings about the future should be labeled as warnings. Experts disagree about how likely and how severe such scenarios may be. One company called an assessed risk very low but not completely negligible. The evidence summarized here does not establish claims about superintelligence, and intelligence explosion, or the singularity. So the current picture is neither nothing is happening, nor AI is already in charge. Capability growth is measured; boundary failures have been observed in special conditions; human monitoring and intervention can work in some cases, but they are not perfect or universal.
